data.narrative:
Karman Industries is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by David Tearse and Chiranjeev Kalra, having raised $11.5M to date. The comparable universe consists of 1 public company (Linz AG, ticker LNZA) and 8 private frontier-tech peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method due to data constraints. The Stage-Progression approach uses the $11.5M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $29M. Peer-Median methodology proved inapplicable: while 8 same-sector peers exist, none satisfied narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers), and a broad sector median would introduce undue noise across heterogeneous business models and development phases.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $24M to $33M, centered at $29M. This range reflects uncertainty inherent in single-method triangulation and the absence of tightly comparable stage-matched comps. Key risks to valuation include execution risk at the Seed stage, technology validation uncertainty typical of frontier-energy companies, and sensitivity to capital market conditions affecting private climate-tech funding.
